The megadomains sit over a small recurrent set of transcription factor loci.

nodes.description: The mechanism-directed approach. Three agents have cached clinical data in this disease, all early phase and all modest: two of four compassionate-use patients responded to OTX015; four of nineteen reached a confirmed or unconfirmed partial response on molibresib; two of eight on RO6870810. A consensus review grades first-generation BET inhibitors as modestly effective in a minority of cases, with a narrow therapeutic window.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Response of Carcinomas Harboring the BRD4-NUT Oncoprotein to the Targeted Bromodomain Inhibitor OTX015/MK-8628.
evidence.snippet: Two patients responded rapidly with tumor regression and symptomatic relief, and a third had meaningful disease stabilization with a minor metabolic response.

evidence.reference_title: Phase 1 Study of Molibresib (GSK525762), a Bromodomain and Extra-Terminal Domain Protein Inhibitor, in NUT Carcinoma and Other Solid Tumors.
evidence.snippet: Among 19 patients with NC, four achieved either confirmed or unconfirmed partial response, eight had stable disease as best response, and four were progression-free for more than 6 months.

evidence.reference_title: A Phase 1 study of RO6870810, a novel bromodomain and extra-terminal protein inhibitor, in patients with NUT carcinoma, other solid tumours, or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
evidence.snippet: Objective response rates were 25% (2/8), 2% (1/47) and 11% (2/19) for patients with NC, other solid tumours and DLBCL, respectively.

evidence.reference_title: Report of the First International Symposium on NUT Carcinoma.
evidence.snippet: It was concluded that standard chemotherapeutic approaches and first-generation BET bromodomain inhibitors, the latter complicated by a narrow therapeutic window, are only modestly effective in a minority of cases.

evidence.snippet: Most patients had the BRD4-NUTM1 fusion (78%), followed by BRD3-NUTM1 (15%) and NSD3-NUTM1 (6%).

nodes.description: The defining cellular consequence. Releasing the block is what the targeted agents aim at: both bromodomain inhibition and histone deacetylase inhibition induce differentiation in cell lines. A variant-fusion study found its own fusion necessary and sufficient for the block, so this is not a BRD4-only mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: The oncogenic BRD4-NUT chromatin regulator drives aberrant transcription within large topological domains.
evidence.snippet: NMC is driven by the creation of a translocation oncoprotein, BRD4-NUT, which blocks differentiation and drives growth of NMC cells.

evidence.reference_title: NSD3-NUT fusion oncoprotein in NUT midline carcinoma: implications for a novel oncogenic mechanism.
evidence.snippet: We find that NSD3-NUT is both necessary and sufficient for the blockade of differentiation and maintenance of proliferation in NMC cells.

evidence.reference_title: Differentiation of NUT midline carcinoma by epigenomic reprogramming.
evidence.snippet: Bulk chromatin acetylation can be restored by treatment of NMC cells with histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACi), engaging a program of squamous differentiation and arrested growth in vitro that closely mimics the effects of siRNA-mediated attenuation of BRD4-NUT expression.

evidence.reference_title: Brd4::Nutm1 fusion gene initiates NUT carcinoma in vivo.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrated that the mouse t(2;17) syntenic chromosome translocation, forming the Brd4::Nutm1 fusion gene, could induce aggressive carcinomas in mice.

nodes.description: The two cached readings of what the fusion does to acetylation are not in conflict and both are recorded. Bulk histone acetylation falls and transcription is repressed, while the megadomains are hyperacetylated expanses. An entry quoting either alone would read as contradicting the other.

evidence.reference_title: Differentiation of NUT midline carcinoma by epigenomic reprogramming.
evidence.snippet: In both gain-of and loss-of-expression assays, we find that expression of BRD4-NUT is associated with globally decreased histone acetylation and transcriptional repression.

evidence.reference_title: The oncogenic BRD4-NUT chromatin regulator drives aberrant transcription within large topological domains.
evidence.snippet: BRD4-NUT forms distinctive nuclear foci in patient tumors, which we found correlate with ∼100 unprecedented, hyperacetylated expanses of chromatin that reach up to 2 Mb in size.

nodes.description: The defining lesion: a translocation fusing NUTM1 to a partner gene. BRD4 is the partner in about 70 to 80 per cent of cases, BRD3 in 15 to 20 and NSD3 in about 6. The normal NUTM1 product is expressed only in testis, so the fusion puts a germ-cell protein under a ubiquitously expressed partner's control.

nodes.description: The NUT half recruits and activates p300, and the complex builds contiguous hyperacetylated chromatin domains that reach two megabases. These megadomains are mostly lineage-specific, but three stem-cell transcription factors are targeted across tumours and tissues.
